questions.stem: A season has one crew, two months and one 6-week trim. What does the month model answer, and why?

options.text: Trimmed in month 1, as the season holds 8 crew-weeks
options.says: The output shows the month model answering 'not trimmed'.

options.text: Trimmed in months 1 and 2, three weeks in each of them
options.says: The month model books a trim in one month only; it answered 'not trimmed'.

options.text: Trimmed in month 2, after the crew has finished month 1
options.says: The output shows the month model answering 'not trimmed'.

options.text: Not trimmed, as no single month holds 6 crew-weeks
options.says: Right: one crew's month holds 4 crew-weeks, so no month can take the trim.

origin.section: The Month Model Promises Work One Crew Cannot Do, and Refuses Work One Crew Can

questions.stem: In the interval model, C04's optional interval on crew K2 has its presence literal false. What does K2's NoOverlap do with that interval?

options.text: It keeps the interval from sharing weeks with K2's other trims
options.says: An inactive interval is simply ignored by all constraints, NoOverlap included.

options.text: It ignores it, since an absent interval takes part in nothing
options.says: Right: the docstring says an inactive interval is simply ignored by all constraints.

options.text: It counts the interval's weeks as busy for crew K2 anyway
options.says: An inactive interval is simply ignored; it occupies no weeks.

options.text: It makes the model infeasible until the literal is set true
options.says: An absent interval is ignored, so it cannot make the model infeasible.

origin.section: A Trim Is an Optional Interval on Each Crew, and a Crew's Intervals Never Overlap

questions.stem: Two tests of the month model leave the suite in this step. What reason does the lesson give?

options.text: They checked the budget row, which the new model drops
options.says: The budget row stays in the interval model.

options.text: Their crew rule no longer applies to the new season
options.says: Their rule survives in new tests.

options.text: They checked a time unit, which the new model no longer has
options.says: Right: they retire because months no longer exist; their rule survives in new tests.

options.text: They read each trim's crew, which the new model drops
options.says: The new model keeps a crew on every trim: Trim replaces month with a crew, a first week and an end week.

origin.section: Five New Tests, and Two Old Ones Retire
